epoch_ai.synthesis: Oct 26: Epoch's 'We tried to automate Epoch' reports that its Automation Reports, tasks Epoch staff do regularly (graphic design, planning research projects), were scored against the rubric items a human employee would be judged on. The leaders, Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra, averaged 65%; 100% would mean the task can be handed over, so every task would have been rejected or revised from a human. AIs did better on clearly defined work (coding, data analysis) than on open-ended judgment. GPT-6 Astra set a pilot experiment's token budget too low, so 22% of runs returned no answer, then treated that as a finding about the models. One task has already crossed the threshold and moved to AI. Epoch cautions 65% does not mean 65% of the way to automation. Read from the feed's summary of the longer report; who wrote the rubrics, and when, is in the report and was not read. Oct 9 InnovationEval (best result 15% of SDPO's gains) is the earlier reading. The cron's Epoch pull is 403-blocked; fetched directly.

semianalysis.synthesis: Oct 23: SemiAnalysis says Anthropic runs production inference and RL rollouts on Amazon's Trainium2 and Trainium3; Trainium has been good at inference and not the best fit for research training, and the piece argues it is now reaching for training. Oct 19 (earlier): 2027 as a year of about 50 GW of datacenter capacity added. Read from feed summaries only (paywalled); the capacity figure comes from SemiAnalysis's own models, method undisclosed.

farmdoc_daily.synthesis: Oct 23: Zulauf and Monaco find the nine cost-of-production crops lost $28.1 billion at harvest in 2025 and the US crop safety net covered all but $3.7 billion; over 2023-2025, $62.5 billion in safety net payments left the nine crops a combined net return of $0.20 billion. They conclude it is hard to argue the sector is in financial distress and warn that removing losses can weaken efficiency and make cropland more attractive as an investment. The article does not split coverage by program. Oct 20: Illinois farm diesel hit a record $5.76 a gallon on Oct 16 (USDA AMS), adding about $6 an acre to central Illinois corn fuel and oil, now about $28. Oct 27 (summary only): Mexican feeder cattle imports have been halted since 2025 by New World screwworm; a partial reopening is in effect and its effect on beef markets is uncertain.

drought_monitor.synthesis: Indiana as of Oct 20: 51.1% abnormally dry (D0), up from 18.8% on Oct 13, and still 0.0% in moderate drought (D1). D0 coverage has gone 3.2% (Sept 22), 10.0%, 11.2%, 18.8%, 51.1%; no D1 in any week this fall. The Oct 27 map was not yet in the pull.

nass_crop_progress.synthesis: Week ending Oct 25, Indiana: corn 61% harvested for grain (46% a week earlier, 34% two weeks earlier); soybeans 75% harvested (59%, 44%). This week's pull carries harvest only, not maturity or leaf-drop.

interconnection_fyi.synthesis: Indiana holds 56 tracked data-center projects (33 proposed, 13 cancelled, 6 under construction, 4 operational), unchanged in all 41 snapshots since Sept 12 (latest Oct 27). Lake (9) and Porter (7) counties lead.

noaa_ncei_monthly.synthesis: September 2026, Indiana, revised slightly (651 station-months, from 646): 71.1°F average and 3.2 in. precipitation, against 73.0°F and 7.2 in. for August; Michigan 62.2°F and 3.2 in. The pull carries no normals; MRCC's regional figure (+4.9°F) gives the departure.

equitable_growth.synthesis: Oct 23: Equitable Growth assesses Sen. Wyden's Stability and Opportunity for Workers Act: a 26-week minimum UI duration at 75% wage replacement, automatic Extended Benefits of up to 52 weeks when national unemployment rises, lower earnings thresholds, a federal job-seekers allowance, and 26 weeks of benefits for full-time training. It reports the share of unemployed workers receiving benefits fell from over 50% in the 1950s to under 30% recently, and Florida and Arizona replace under 15% of average weekly wages. It also says the research on AI's labor market effects is mixed and gives no measured AI job-loss figure, so the AI case for the bill rests on scenario planning. Earlier, Oct 5: an argued piece on the budget (FY2026 revenue just under 17% of GDP, spending about 23%).

ipcc.synthesis: Oct 16: the Chair suspended the 65th Plenary in Addis Ababa after it overran and many delegations from least developed countries and small island states had left. The Panel agreed most items, including a process for using AI, but not the timelines for the three AR7 Working Group reports or the budget. It will reconvene 'at the earliest opportunity'; no date was given.

beige_book.synthesis: Oct 14, Chicago District: activity was flat on balance in late August and September, after rising slightly in the Sept 2 report. Consumer spending was flat; construction, real estate and business spending fell slightly; prices rose moderately and wages modestly; farm income expectations for 2026 fell slightly, after improving in September. Nationally, most Districts saw little or no change in consumer spending, and over half said spending was driven by high-income households.

indiana_dnr_water.synthesis: Indiana DNR, September: statewide rainfall 91% of normal, after 200% in August. Ten of 12 tracked streams ran above normal; the Muscatatuck River near Deputy was lowest at 16% of mean monthly flow. Groundwater was above normal at 4 of 9 wells, near normal at 3, and well below at LaGrange 2 and Clark 20. The seasonal outlook shows no drought through at least December.

fia_indiana.synthesis: USFS 2025 evaluation for Indiana: 4.83M acres of forest, 14.07B cu ft growing stock. Annual mortality is 1.18% of standing volume (sampling error 5.5%), essentially level with 1.19% in the 2024 evaluation; net growth is 2.23%. First reading in this series.

mrcc_monthly_summary.synthesis: September 2026: Midwest average 68.5°F, 4.9°F above the 1991-2020 normal, with the whole region above normal (August was +0.9°F). Read from the feed's opening paragraph; the MRCC site has returned errors on several pulls since Oct 18.

interconnection_fyi_national.synthesis: Across 46 US state pages the largest active pipelines are Virginia (329), Texas (282) and Ohio (86); Indiana is 4th at 39 (4.0% of 972) but 32nd in operating sites (4 of 2,435). These ranks are unchanged in every snapshot since at least Oct 20. The tracker's own headline count moved on Oct 24 (12,538 to 13,027 records) with no change on the state pages, and still does not reconcile with them, so read ranks as rough.

epoch_datacenters.synthesis: Dataset updated Oct 26: still 95 covered sites and 14.2 GW; the US rose to 12.01 GW (from 11.98), 84%. Indiana is 1.22 GW, 8.5% of the covered total (Anthropic-Amazon New Carlisle 1,037 MW, Meta Jeffersonville 178 MW). Covered set only, not world capacity.

ohchr_ukraine_civilians.synthesis: September 2026: the UN monitoring mission verified at least 328 civilians killed and 2,105 injured, 85% more than in September 2025, with casualties on 22 of the month's 30 days. Its head, Danielle Bell, said the first two weeks of October were among the deadliest periods for civilians in years. July had been the highest month since March 2022. Counts are verified cases and are revised upward later. Read via UN News; the OHCHR site refuses scripted fetches.

ochaopt_gaza.synthesis: Oct 21 snapshot: 74,494 Palestinians reported killed since October 2023 (74,237 identified as of Oct 7), up from 74,392 on Oct 14; figures are Gaza Ministry of Health and Israeli-authority numbers the UN has not verified. The Oct 22 report gives 1,522 killed and 5,421 injured since the October 2025 ceasefire, with 32 killed and 123 injured Oct 13-19 and 67 deaths added retroactively. Food: monthly assistance reached about 1.3 million people in September, against 2.1 million in January, with rations about half of minimum caloric needs and partners expecting under 1 million a month from October. First half of October: 710 of 24,499 children screened (3%) admitted for acute malnutrition, 102 severe. Commercial truck entries fell 25% to 315 in Oct 12-18, with reports of an import halt tied to a fee charged by the de facto authorities. The report does not state ceasefire terms.

ofac_sdn.synthesis: List of Oct 21, unchanged at Oct 27: 19,471 entries; 6,733 carry a Russia or Ukraine program tag, 4,070 an Iran tag, 3,360 SDGT (counter-terrorism, which covers Hamas but is not Gaza-specific). A standing count: designations raise it and delistings lower it, so it reads week against week.

kiel_tracker.synthesis: Release 31 (Oct 8) adds aid announced through August 2026. Its headline is Germany: of the EUR 100 billion Germany reports as bilateral aid, about 41.7 billion counts as aid to Ukraine under Kiel's method, 35.9 billion was spent in Germany, largely on Ukrainian refugees, and 22.0 billion is future military commitments. Donor totals are in the release file and were not read this session.

ice_detention.synthesis: ICE's latest file (FY2026, data as of July 9, file dated July 20): 65,765 people in detention, 19,329 convicted of a crime, 20,247 with charges pending and 26,189 with immigration violations only, so 70.6% with no criminal conviction. ICE's detention page, updated Oct 27, still links the file dated July 20, more than three months old. Fetched directly; ice.gov refuses the cron runner.

press_freedom_tracker.synthesis: 253 incidents against journalists from Jan 1 to Oct 27, 2026, against 278 in the same span of 2025, not counting chilling statements. Assaults lead (168), then arrests or criminal charges (44) and equipment damage (31); subpoenas or legal orders 22. Latest incident dated Oct 21; the count was 250 on Oct 22.

atlas_surveillance.synthesis: First reading: 15,135 records of police surveillance technology across 7,761 agencies. Body-worn cameras 5,470, license-plate readers 4,094, drones 1,828, face recognition 980. Indiana: 410 records, of which 216 are license-plate readers, 110 body cameras and 38 drones. Slow-moving; an unchanged count is expected.

fec_money.synthesis: 2026 cycle through Sept 30: PACs, super PACs included, raised $11.08 billion and spent $4.25 billion; candidates raised $3.09 billion and parties $1.85 billion. PAC money is not limited to independent expenditures, and spending by groups that do not disclose donors cannot be separated in this series.

justsecurity_litigation.synthesis: 984 court challenges to administration actions tracked, from the tracker page published Oct 26, up from 983 on Oct 20 and 981 on Oct 12. The tracker's rules count an appeal with its case and some groups of related suits as one; its status totals still read 'update in progress'. Fetched directly; the site refuses the cron runner.

ccc_protests.synthesis: Data through May 2026 (Dataverse version of Sept 10): 4,534 protest events in May, after 6,226 in January, 3,343 in February, 6,620 in March and 3,284 in April. Indiana: 128 in May, between 107 and 180 each month since December. The data runs about four months behind.
